newsitem.title: USA: Bill calls for Minn. to pay all school operations.
newsitem.headline: Bill calls for Minn. to pay all school operations.

text.p: A bipartisan group of Minnesota state lawmakers introduced a bill Monday that would require the state to pay 100 percent of operating costs for elementary and secondary public schools.

State Rep. Ann Rest, D-New Hope, a leading proponent of the bill, said the plan, estimated to cost $2.1 billion, would eliminate all local school operating property taxes, replacing some of those revenues with a state property tax.
In addition, the bill would restructure the state aid formula for other local governments based on need in order to save state dollars that could be used for schools, she explained.
Rest said some money from the estimated $1.4 billion state budget surplus expected at the end of the upcoming bienium could also be used for schools.

The state property tax is estimated to raise nearly $1.2 billion, while restructuring the state aid formula for aid would save $566 million, according to materials explaining the plan. Another $357 million could be used from the projected state surplus.
Further property tax relief would be provided by a switch to voter-approved local income taxes from property tax levy referendums for school discretionary spending.

School property tax levies for existing long-term debt for capital projects would remain in place, according to a fiscal analyst for the House. Meanwhile, state aid would replace alternative facilities property tax levies supporting school bonds, the analyst said.
Rest said that the bill would not raise any state taxes and would take effect in fiscal 2000.

"Overall property taxes will be reduced by more than 12 percent and the new system will be structured to permanently reduce reliance on property taxes," Rest said. "This proposal acknowledges the need for greater fairness in our property tax system and the responsibility of the state to provide equitable, stable funding for all Minnesota public schools."
The state currently pays about 60 percent of school costs, according to Rest.
